TIKTOK WORKFLOW

The workflow this page is built for

TikTok delivery works when it feels immediate, spoken, and native to the feed. A polished paragraph often sounds like an advertisement, while overlays can cover important words or gestures. CuePrompt helps shape a conversational hook, quick proof, and a vertical recording that respects screen safe areas.

From hook to vertical export

  1. Choose the TikTok template and write the hook as something you would genuinely say to one person.
  2. Build the middle from short claims, demonstrations, or cuts; mark where on-screen text and B-roll will appear.
  3. Rehearse without memorizing, record in 9:16, then check caption placement and the final call to action in preview.

Recommended CuePrompt settings

  • Keep each prompt line to one spoken thought and use Smart Follow when you want flexible reactions.
  • Place the reading area near the lens but away from the lower caption zone and right-side controls.
  • Use [pause] for cuts or demonstrations and [slow] only where a key phrase needs emphasis.

A short-video structure that fits

Conversational hook → name the frustration → show the proof or process → concise takeaway → comment, save, or follow action.

“If you keep re-recording the same opening, try this. [pause] Say the problem exactly as your viewer would say it, then show the fix before you explain why it works.”

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Writing formal marketing copy that does not sound natural when spoken.
  • Placing captions or product details where interface controls will cover them.
  • Using a generic “follow for more” before giving viewers a concrete payoff.

Questions before you record

Should I read every word exactly?

Usually not. Keep the hook and key claim precise, but treat supporting lines as prompts so your delivery stays conversational.

Where should captions go?

Keep essential text away from the bottom edge and platform controls. Always inspect the exported video in a vertical preview before posting.

Can I plan cuts in the script?

Yes. Add [pause] where you will change angle, demonstrate an action, or insert B-roll so the recording leaves clean edit points.
